title: The three squares theorem (Gauss–Legendre)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the three squares theorem of Legendre (1798) and Gauss (1801): a natural number is a sum of three squares if and only if it is not of the form 4^a (8 b + 7) (sum_three_sq_iff), with the corollary that every n ≡ 3 (mod 8) is x₀² + x₁² + x₂² for some x : Fin 3 → ℤ (exists_sum_sq_of_mod_eight_eq_three). The proof uses ternary quadratic forms of determinant one: a positive definite integral ternary form of determinant one is equivalent to x² + y² + z² (proved with Minkowski's convex body theorem), and for n ≢ 0 (mod 4), n ≢ 7 (mod 8) such a form with diagonal entry n is built from a prime in an arithmetic progression (Dirichlet's theorem, as in Mathlib) and quadratic reciprocity for the Jacobi symbol. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
